fingerprint.session: CachyOS/KDE Plasma 6 Wayland, RS3 NXT via XWayland
fingerprint._note: Regions are pixel offsets measured on this exact window size. At any other size they resolve elsewhere and fail silently - OCR returns nothing, or reads a neighbouring panel. ui_scale 1.75 is the logical-to-physical factor KWin reports (2194 logical vs 3840 pixels); `doctor` detects it independently and reports it.

window._comment: RS3 NXT. WM_CLASS survives title changes and skips the Steam launcher window.

_profile_note: Basic Woodcutting profile: three alerts only - pack about to fill, chopping stopped, and the one-hour session milestone. Regions are reused verbatim from the fishing profile, which is safe because RS3 pins these panels to the window edges at a fixed size: the backpack, chat and Metrics panel sit in exactly the same place whatever skill is being trained. Verified here rather than assumed - `doctor` resolves every region and the occupancy grid was checked against the live pack.
_regions_help: anchor + dx,dy offset from that corner + fixed w,h. RS3 pins panels to edges at fixed size rather than scaling them, so this survives a window resize. Negative dx/dy measure inward from a right/bottom edge.

chat_tail._note: Most recent ~32 lines of All Chat. Taken from the thieving profile rather than fishing's smaller box: woodcutting produces a log line roughly every 2-3s, so the taller region gives each line many more chances to be read before it scrolls off. dy=-36 is the largest offset that still excludes the chat input bar below it; at -57 the boundary falls mid-line and the NEWEST message - the one rules care about most - OCRs as garbage.

backpack._note: Full backpack panel; grid is relative to the region's top-left. VERIFIED live while chopping maples: per-cell occupancy signal read 21-47 for slots holding logs and 0.8-4.1 for empty ones, so the threshold of 8 sits far from both populations. The grid describes 5x6=30 cells while the pack holds 28; the two surplus cells are always empty and are simply never counted as occupied.

session_timer._note: Elapsed-time readout at the bottom of the Metrics panel, between the settings/reset buttons on the left and pause on the right. Same geometry as every other profile - RS3 pins the panel top-left at a fixed size. Re-check with `shot session_timer` if the Metrics panel is moved or resized.

rules.name: pack_nearly_full
rules._wood_box_note: min_occupancy exists because of the Magic wood box. Clicking it stores logs in batches, so the pack empties mid-grind without any banking - MEASURED live: occupancy ran 7 -> 1 -> 7 -> 2 -> 10 -> 20 inside 50 seconds. The evaluator treats any drop of more than 2 slots as a bank trip and clears the fill-rate history, so the rapid gains straight after a box store look like an explosive fill rate. Replaying that exact sequence through the rule fired '18 slots left - bank soon' at 10/28 and then disarmed itself all the way to 27/28: it cried wolf early and was silent when the pack really was about to fill. Requiring 18 occupied before a PROJECTION may fire turns that into a correct warning at 20/28 with 8 slots left. warn_free=3 is unaffected - it reads the live count, which is true whatever the history says, so a genuine near-full pack still alerts even if the projection is suppressed.
rules._note: Advance warning: fires when the projected time-to-full drops below lead_seconds, so it arrives while there is still time to act rather than after chopping has already stopped. lead_seconds=20 and warn_free=3 against a measured log rate of roughly one every 2-3s - three free slots is about 6-9 seconds of chopping, so the projection and the slot floor agree with each other. Deliberately paired with nothing: the fishing and thieving profiles also carry an 'overflow' backstop rule, but this is a basic profile and two inventory alerts per bank trip is the noise problem those profiles had to be retuned away from. If a full pack is being missed, add an overflow rule rather than lowering lead_seconds.

rules.name: woodcutting_stopped
rules.suppress_pattern: can'?t carry any more|do not have any space in your inventory|not have any space|your backpack is full
rules.alert_body: No logs for {quiet:.0f}s - chopping has stopped.
rules._note: Fires when all evidence of chopping stops - the tree was felled, the pack filled, or the character was moved. VERIFIED against live chat while cutting maples: the two real lines are 'You get some maple logs.' and 'You swing your hatchet at the tree.'. The 'g?' in 'you g?et' is NOT a typo. MEASURED over 852 live lines: tesseract drops the g and reads 'You et some maple logs' often enough that the strict spelling matched only 71% of them, while 'you g?et some \w+ logs' reached 90% and adding the hatchet line covered 100%. A rule that misses three lines in ten would keep declaring a stop mid-chop. '\w+' rather than 'maple' so the rule survives a move to a different tree. suppress_pattern is essential for the same reason it is in the fishing profile: a full pack halts chopping outright, so log messages stop on EVERY bank trip - without it this rule fires once per trip, which is exactly the once-per-cycle noise the other profiles had to be retuned to avoid. pack_nearly_full already reports that case. stop_seconds=45 against a log arriving every 2-3s leaves a very wide margin for a garbled OCR run; lower it to ~20 if a faster stop report matters more than tolerance for unreadable frames.

rules.name: session_hour
rules._note: Reads the Metrics panel's own elapsed timer rather than tracking wall-clock time in the watcher. That is the better source: it is the number already on screen, it pauses when the player pauses it, and it survives a watcher restart because the game owns it. step=3600 fires once per hour. The parser anchors on [0-5] for the minute and second fields so a garbled frame like '00:82:09' is rejected rather than becoming a bogus elapsed time, and a timer reset rewinds the milestone counter so a fresh session starts clean.

_notification_note: Rules use urgency 'normal' with an explicit timeout_ms so KDE auto-dismisses them. Setting urgency to 'critical' makes KDE keep the popup until it is closed by hand and ignore timeout_ms - only do that for an alert you must not miss.
